Bug_Details:
Don't create instances of already existing BigInteger (`BigInteger.ZERO`, `BigInteger.ONE`),
for Java 1.5 onwards, BigInteger.TEN and BigDecimal (`BigDecimal.ZERO`, `BigDecimal.ONE`, `BigDecimal.TEN`) and
for Java 9 onwards `BigInteger.TWO`.
Examples:
BigInteger bi1 = new BigInteger("1");    // reference BigInteger.ONE instead
BigInteger bi2 = new BigInteger("0");    // reference BigInteger.ZERO instead
BigInteger bi3;
bi3 = new BigInteger("0");               // reference BigInteger.ZERO instead

BigDecimal bd1 = new BigDecimal(0);      // reference BigDecimal.ZERO instead
BigDecimal bd2 = new BigDecimal("0.") ;  // reference BigDecimal.ZERO instead
BigDecimal bd3 = new BigDecimal(10);     // reference BigDecimal.TEN instead
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by explicitly instantiating BigInteger and BigDecimal objects with values that already have predefined constants in Java. Specifically, BigInteger("1"), BigInteger("0"), BigDecimal(0), BigDecimal("0."), and BigDecimal(10) are used instead of BigInteger.ONE, BigInteger.ZERO, BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal.ZERO, and BigDecimal.TEN respectively.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by calling the methods showBug1, showBug2, showBug3, showBug4, and showBug5 of the BigIntegerInstantiationBug class. These methods instantiate BigInteger and BigDecimal objects using string literals and integer values instead of using the predefined constants like BigInteger.ONE, BigInteger.ZERO, BigDecimal.ZERO, and BigDecimal.TEN.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that all tests passed successfully without any failures. This indicates that the methods in the Java code are returning the expected values (BigInteger.ONE, BigInteger.ZERO, BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal.TEN), which means the bug was not triggered as the incorrect instantiation did not affect the outcome of the tests.
